options: Structuring data so that changes over time are explicitly captured and preserved
Structuring data around measurable facts and descriptive dimensions
Structuring data as nodes and edges for traversal
Structuring data as message contracts between services
questions.explanation: Temporal models record how data has evolved instead of only its current state, enabling questions about the past, present and even planned future states.

questions.stem: What does Valid Time refer to in temporal modelling?
options: When the fact was recorded in the system
When a fact is true in the real world
When the database was last backed up
questions.explanation: Valid Time is when a fact is true in the real world, for example an interest rate valid from January to March.

questions.stem: What does Transaction Time refer to in temporal modelling?
options: When the fact is true in the business world
When the fact was recorded in the system
questions.explanation: Transaction Time is when the fact was recorded in the system; a correction entered in February about a January event has a different transaction time from its valid time.

questions.stem: What is a model called when it captures both Valid Time and Transaction Time?
questions.explanation: When both valid time and transaction time are captured together, the model is called bi-temporal.

questions.stem: What is the key principle governing updates in a temporal model?
options: Rows are updated in place and the old value discarded
Rows are deleted and reinserted with new values
Only the latest value is kept in a cache
Changes are stored in a separate audit log only
Data is never overwritten; new versions are inserted with time boundaries
questions.explanation: Instead of updating a row in place, new versions are inserted carrying attributes such as ValidFrom and ValidTo, preserving a complete timeline.

questions.stem: In the temporal loan timeline for Loan L001, what happens on 1 February 2024?
options: The interest rate is corrected to 8.0%, stored as a new time slice
The loan is submitted with status Pending
questions.explanation: On 1 February 2024 the rate is corrected to 8.0%; the corrected rate does not erase history but adds another time-bound record while the earlier version remains intact.

questions.stem: Which of the following is an example of an "as-of" query enabled by temporal modelling?
options: Total loan amount approved by branch
Show the loan status as of 14 January 2024
Count of loans per customer segment
List all officers in the Central branch
questions.explanation: Temporal models support as-of queries such as showing the loan status on 14 January 2024 or which rate was valid on 20 January 2024.

questions.stem: With which normal-form principles do temporal tables frequently align when attributes change independently over time?
questions.explanation: Temporal tables often require careful decomposition, frequently aligning with 5NF or 6NF principles, especially when attributes change independently.

questions.stem: Which of the following is NOT listed as a strength of Temporal Data Modelling?
options: Support for regulatory and compliance requirements
questions.explanation: Temporal modelling introduces additional storage and design complexity, and queries become more sophisticated because they must account for time dimensions.

questions.stem: Which industries are named as needing to show what data looked like at a specific point in time?
questions.explanation: Banking, insurance, healthcare and government are named as industries where organisations must demonstrate what data looked like at a specific point in time.
